newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition, SPD meet again on tax.
newsitem.headline: German coalition, SPD meet again on tax.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday began talks with the Social Democrat (SPD) opposition in what was seen by both sides as a last chance to reach an early compromise on tax reforms.

Going into the talks at the federal chancellery, SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said it would be possible to agree on some points "within half an hour", but there were others where there was no hope of reaching a consensus.
The two sides were to discuss a 30 billion mark package of income and corporate tax cuts put together by Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
The main part of the reform, the 1999 tax bill, was approved on Tuesday by Kohl's cabinet and the three parties in his coalition, and will be introduced to parliament on Friday.

Lafontaine, whose party can block the tax measures through its control of the upper house of parliament, said agreement could be reached quickly on cutting the bottom rate of income tax, corporate taxes and jobs insurance contributions.

But he said there would be no deal with the SPD on Waigel's plan to slash the top rate of income tax. "If we put to one side questions we cannot agree on, a reform is possible which doesn't turn against the people," Lafontaine told reporters.
